entities.name: PCOS
observations: Polycystic ovary syndrome; age-related androgen trajectories are the focus of the evidence review.

entities.name: PCOS testosterone decline
observations: In a 13-year prospective cohort of 41 PCOS women and 43 matched controls, total testosterone declined more in PCOS, but PCOS women retained higher total testosterone, free-androgen index, and DHEAS at follow-up.

Cross-sectional studies in 602 and 256 PCOS patients found generally higher androgenicity in younger women, with lower testosterone-related measures, DHEAS, or FAI with age; direct free-testosterone results were sparse.
Postmenopausal PCOS women retained higher total testosterone, DHEAS, and FAI and lower SHBG than matched controls, indicating persistence rather than normalization of androgen excess.

Overall evidence supports an age-related testosterone decrease in PCOS, but certainty is moderate because most studies are observational, age groups and menopause status are heterogeneous, and assay/free-testosterone reporting is incomplete.
